title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 1TB $1800, S26 Plus 512GB $1300 Delivered @ Phonex
body:
Deal: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 1TB $1800, S26 Plus 512GB $1300 Delivered @ Phonex

[Zeee] Can anyone give reviews about this website? I never received any response from them?
[champlooo] Purchased an s26 plus previously from them no issues. Shipped and arrived in a few days. Never had to message them so can't comment on that.
[2pro4sho] Ever had to claim warranty through Samsung Australia? It would not be recognised. This is a grey import. They said warranty handled locally meaning directly through them rather than Samsung. Their description and claims are misleading.
[howcan] What evidence is there that these are grey imported?
[cutsdeep] @howcan: PhoneX is an Australian-owned Online retailer based in Sydney, shipping the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Australia-wide from local stock. Every device is brand new, factory unlocked, and works on Telstra, Optus, Vodafone and every Australian MVNO — no SIM-locked imports, no grey-market handsets.
from their page, seems legit?
[2pro4sho] @cutsdeep: Every grey importer makes the same claim. It is not Australian stock. They are not an authorised Australian Samsung reseller. It is not an Australian imei number. The warranty is not regonised through Samsung Australia.
[howcan] @2pro4sho: Give us evidence of non-Australian IMEI's being sold.
[jimojr] @2pro4sho: They might buy brand new phones from people and resell them, like Mobile Guru or Mobile Monster. So you can't assume the phones aren't Australian stock or don't come with an Australian warranty.
[Froot Loops] @howcan: There aren't an authorised reseller, therefore not getting their stock via Samsung Australia. This means they are grey imports. You should also be asking the seller to provide evidence that they are Australia stock. If you email them requesting this, they will not reply.
[Fuzor] He just wrote its Australian stock.
And the nanny state policy of not providing any service to grey market products is so typically Australian. You can go to most other countries on holidays and get your samsung galaxy batteries replaced by the authorised store there by not vise versa in Australia
[freefall101] They said warranty handled locally meaning directly through them rather than Samsung
That is not what "locally" means.
Are you just using your own interpretation of their website or do you actually have anything to back up your claims? Store has been around for a while now, I couldn't find any complaints online about them selling grey imports.
[howcan] @freefall101: All his claims are nonsensical and he hasn't posted a shred of evidence to support anything that he's claimed. All he's done is double down and start using a fake account to post more nonsense. He's either a troll or working for a competitor of this store. Hard to tell what his motive is for posting all this rubbish.
[OZBsince2018] @howcan: Instead of arguing, those who already purchased from them can get on chat with Samsung, provide either model, serial or IMEI number to them and confirm if these are Australian stock or not. Probably do it before opening the box in case it turns out grey import and can be returned.
[WandP] Bought from them before. No issues. Took about a week to arrive.
[Froot Loops] Have you made a warranty claim directly via Samsung Australia?
[2pro4sho] You're not an official reseller for Samsung. How can you offer Australian warranty? This would not be recognised as warranty from Samsung
[howcan] They have their own warranty/repair process. It doesn't need to go back to Samsung.
[2pro4sho] This is NOT Australian stock as they claim. I have an issue with their false claims. This is a grey import and if they are not around in 12 months good luck with getting warranty claim fixed.
[howcan] What evidence do you have these are grey import/not Aus stock? Please share it.
[2pro4sho] @howcan: Not on the Samsung approved reseller list. They offer "local" warranty. Anything else you need mate? If it's not regonised as Australian warranty via Samsung, what makes it Australian stock? Because it's now physically located in Australia?
[howcan] @2pro4sho: Just because they're not an official reseller doesn't mean their stock isn't Australian distributed stock. You don't seem to have a clue how distribution channels work. You're acting like a complete clown at the moment, grandstanding and making claims with zero evidence to mislead everyone.
[wigglypuff] @howcan: you’re delusional if you think this is australian stock
[howcan] @wigglypuff: Interesting. The only people claiming it isn't AU stock, with zero evidence, is a lonely Pokemon card fanatic, and a fake sockpuppet account of the Pokemon fanatic.
[wigglypuff] @howcan: a website like this can be made in 20 mins stating anything they want
[wigglypuff] @howcan: certainly wouldn’t purchase something through this site worth over a grand
[Blitzfx] Can you share their step by step warranty repair process that doesn't involve Samsung?
[Kegsta] Still more expensive than the March preorder deal.
[OZBsince2018] Ome who wants to buy now, unfortunately, can't time travel to March. And we all know no subsequent deals usually can beat the Samsung pre-order deals.
[Chance] How much one would expect to spend on fold 8 ultra 1TB?
[Keeegs] Oh looks like they're having a promo for the fold 8 Ultra too in another thread: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/979477
But yes, the 256GB is around $1800+ as the best price. Not sure of the 1TB
[howcan] They're an Australian business you liar 🤦‍♂️
[Froot Loops] Being an Australian business doesn't mean they are selling authorised local Samsung stock. I don't think you understand why a grey import or a non-authorised product is.
[howcan] You're the one that claimed the store isn't local. I don't think you even know what you're even posting.
[Juandimr] I'm not associated with them but bought a Galaxy S25 Ultra about 1.5 years ago (March 2025). Sadly a few months ago (Sept 2026) the wide lenses camera stopped focusing and was making a clicky noise. I took it directly to Samsung Chermside in Brisbane and didn't bother contacting PhoneX.
At the beginning they were super sus about it when I provided my PhoneX invoice and said they were not sure if they could service it for me because it wasn't bought from an authorised reseller. I insisted that PhoneX in their emails said they were "Samsung One B2B Partner" and I had proof of those emails and showed them to Samsung. They were still skeptical so they contacted the official repair shop and they accepted the device because they checked the IMEI and it was Australian stock and it was within the manufactured warranty period.
I honestly don't know if they are legit or not, they warned me to avoid buying from them and that they will investigate if they are legit or if they are faking this. To be honest this experience left a bad taste for me so I probably won't buy from them again. I'll just always wait for the preorder deals and that's it. They are better anyway
[Blitzfx] I looked them up and they have a legit ABN, but I wouldn't trust a $2k phone with them because they have no reputation and they've changed ABNs before.
They were originally registered under ABN 27617310175 since 10 Feb 2017, and with entity name FONESOLUTION BLACKTOWN PTY LTD, and Business name PhoneX
However, their website now shows ABN 65695985829, registered since 7th March 2026 this year, under entity name TECVANTA PTY LTD, same business name PhoneX
The original ABN was issued a notice by ASIC for deregistration
If you were curious, this is what s601AB(1) or (1A) means
So what this would have meant in the past is that, if you had a dispute with PhoneX, you would have to provide the ABN, but since they changed ABNs, the next task would then be for you to PROVE illegal Phoenixing, that the two entities are the same.
[tasty-falafel] ⛔Virtual neg - Samsung has terrible build quality and is a complete pain to deal with for any warranty claims, even when under 3 years.
